Shipping MAILING LIST Contact Back to site REDRUM V2 $ 139.00 1 of 2 Select option Select option TWO WEEK BUILD TIME Qty $ 139.00 Add to cart View cart The original Redrum was a RAT style distortion running into a maxed out HM-2 style tone stack, with one knob for distortion control and an internal volume control. This revamped version has much more control up top and internally. The original DRIVE knob is still there but now the GRIND and LEVEL controls give you more tone and volume options on the fly! Plus there is an internal DIP switch bank where each of the High, Mid and Low of the original tone stack can each separately be set for min/max or to be controled by the GRIND knob!! Plug this sucker in and you'll be hauting hotels in no time!!! SPECS: 4.7" x 2.6" x 1.5" 125B sized enclosure, true bypass switching, common 9-18vdc "CENTER NEGATIVE" 2.1mm BOSS style power input. Current draw ?mA. Power supply not included. TESTIMONIALS: "The Redrum V2 came in today and I love this pedal! The extra controls make getting so many different flavors way easier than the first version. It has grit and grind and chomp! Definitely an all around improvement. Also, the artwork is an improvement as well. The first versions' art was great, but this is even better. I wouldn't change a thing. It is an awesome pedal." -Colt H. (Louisiana) "I plugged in the Redrum, and as expected, it sounds evil enough to make Satan blush!" -Jeremy H. (California) "So far I’m really digging this pedal. The RAT is my favorite type of distortion, as I generally play punk, metal or doom, so I like the range. I’ve tried this with my Gibson SG in standard tuning, and my Epiphone Les Paul in C Standard tuning, and it sounds great with both!" -Sean G. (Oregon) "V2 is a BLAST to play man! Chugging, palm muting, sweet sweet sweet feedback that goes on and at an absolutely perfect volume for walking it along. It reeeaallly likes the P90's! F'n awesome how much punch is going on in there. Lower gain levels are excellent too. It covers a lot and that's going through a solid state setup. I am using the tone dip switches to the grind knob. Kick ass option there not a gimmick." -Chris Q.
